def-tdmath-van-hove-sequence:
## Definition

For a bounded set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ and $R>0$, define its two-sided boundary layer
$$\partial_R\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)\leq R\},$$
where distance is Euclidean distance and $|\cdot|$ denotes $d$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. A van Hove sequence is a sequence of bounded Lebesgue measurable sets $(\Omega_k)_{k\geq1}$ with $0<|\Omega_k|<\infty$, $|\Omega_k|\to\infty$, and
$$\frac{|\partial_R\Omega_k|}{|\Omega_k|}\longrightarrow0\qquad\text{for every fixed }R>0.$$
The condition controls both inner and outer boundary neighborhoods. It does not impose connectedness, a bounded aspect ratio, smooth boundaries, or a periodic identification.
def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interacti:
## Definition

Assume AC. Fix an integer dimension $d\geq1$, use the Euclidean norm $|\cdot|_2$ from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], define $|x|_\infty=\max_j|x_j|$, and use the numerical coordinate conventions in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. A finite configuration is a finite subset $\omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ with no repeated points; its number of points is $N(\omega)$. A pair potential is an even Borel function, measurable for the Borel sigma-algebra generated by open sets ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]), $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where even means $\phi(-x)=\phi(x)$. Define
$$H_\phi(\omega)=\sum_{\{x,y\}\subset\omega}\phi(x-y),\qquad H_\phi(\varnothing)=0.$$
The sum is over unordered two-point subsets, so every term is evaluated at a nonzero separation; if any term is $+\infty$, the sum is $+\infty$.

The potential is stable if some $B\geq0$ satisfies $H_\phi(\omega)\geq-BN(\omega)$ for every finite configuration. It is superstable in the Georgii splitting convention if $\phi=\phi_s+\phi_r$, where $\phi_s$ is stable and $\phi_r\geq0$ everywhere and, for some $r_0,\delta>0$, $\phi_r(x)\geq\delta$ whenever $|x|_\infty\leq r_0$. It is lower regular if a nonnegative nonincreasing $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,+\infty]$ satisfies
$$\phi(x)\geq-\psi(|x|_\infty),\qquad \int_0^\infty\psi(r)r^{d-1}\,dr<\infty.$$
It is regular if it is lower regular and, for some $R<\infty$, $\phi(x)\leq\psi(|x|_\infty)$ whenever $|x|_\infty\geq R$. These are the conventions used for the interacting results on this page. A genuine divergent positive core is the separate additional condition that some nonincreasing $\chi:(0,r_1]\to(0,\infty)$ satisfies $\phi(x)\geq\chi(|x|_\infty)$ for $0<|x|_\infty\leq r_1$ and $\int_0^{r_1}\chi(r)r^{d-1}dr=+\infty$; it is not implied by superstability.

For $L>0$ put $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, $V_L=L^d$, and let $H_{L,\mathrm{free}}$ be $H_\phi$ for configurations restricted to $\Lambda_L$. For sufficiently large periodic cubes, periodize $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$ by $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and set
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}},\ y\ne x}\phi(y-x),$$
interpreting the value as $+\infty$ if a positive infinite term occurs. The far image sum is absolutely convergent for all sufficiently large $L$ by [[lem-tdmath-integrable-tail-diagonal-gap]]; this is the image convention used below. With fixed numerical length and energy units, the canonical positional partition is
$$Z(L,N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\Lambda_L^N}e^{-\beta H_\phi(q_1,\ldots,q_N)}dq_1\cdots dq_N,\quad Z(L,0;\beta)=1,$$
where $\beta>0$, and the grand partition is $\Xi(L;a,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}a^NZ(L,N;\beta)$ for numerical activity $a>0$. The normalized unit-intensity Poisson version is $Z_Q(L;z,\beta)=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,\mathrm{free}}}]$; since the Poisson density contributes $e^{-V_L}$, $\Xi(L;z,\beta)=e^{V_L}Z_Q(L;z,\beta)$. A physical pressure identification is not part of this mathematical definition.

For a stationary probability law $P$ on the configuration space of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], write $\rho(P)=E_PN_{[0,1)^d}$. When the limit exists, write
$$\mathcal E(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}V_L^{-1}E_PH_{L,\mathrm{free}},\qquad I(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}V_L^{-1}D(P_{\Lambda_L}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_L}).$$
The cited results below establish existence under their stated hypotheses; this definition does not assume it for every stationary law.
def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field:
## Definition

Use the cube $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and the translation $T_x$ defined in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. For a finite configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, let $\omega^{(L)}=\{q+Lk:q\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ be its periodic continuation. Define its **periodized empirical field**
$$R_{L,\omega}:=\frac1{L^d}\int_{\Lambda_L}\delta_{T_x\omega^{(L)}}\,dx.$$
The integral is the push-forward of normalized Lebesgue measure on $\Lambda_L$ under $x\mapsto T_x\omega^{(L)}$. For a probability law $C_L$ on finite configurations in $\Lambda_L$, define its **empirical-field barycenter** $\bar C_L$ by
$$\bar C_L(f):=\int C_L(d\omega)\,R_{L,\omega}(f)=\frac1{L^d}\int_{\Lambda_L}E_{C_L}[f(T_x\omega^{(L)})]\,dx$$
for local tame $f$ from [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]]. This is a spatial average over the finite box, not the raw finite-volume law viewed at a fixed origin.
lem-tdmath-integrable-tail-diagonal-gap:
## Statement

Let $d\geq1$ and let $\phi$ be a regular potential with a nonnegative nonincreasing envelope $\psi:[R_0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, where $R_0<\infty$ and $\int_{R_0}^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)dr<\infty$. Thus $|\phi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|_\infty)$ for $|x|_\infty\geq R_0$. For $g>2R_0$ set
$$\eta(g)=g^d\psi(g)+\int_g^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)dr.$$
Then $\eta(g)\to0$ and
$$\sum_{m=1}^\infty m^{d-1}\psi(mg)\leq 2^{d-1}g^{-d}\eta(g).$$
Moreover, there is a choice $g(\ell)>0$, for all sufficiently large real $\ell$, such that $g(\ell)\to\infty$, $g(\ell)/\ell\to0$, and
$$\left(\frac{\ell}{g(\ell)}\right)^d\eta(g(\ell))\longrightarrow0.$$
For every fixed finite configuration and all sufficiently large periods $L$, the noncoincident periodic-image tail $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d,\ |k|_\infty\geq K_0}|\phi(x-y+Lk)|$ is absolutely convergent. The tail of the cell envelope $\psi(|j|_\infty-1)$ over all sufficiently large integer offsets is summable. This lemma is a deterministic tail estimate; it uses no superstability or thermodynamic-limit conclusion.
lem-tdmath-superstable-cell-energy-bound:
## Statement

Let $\phi=\phi_s+\phi_r$ be superstable in the splitting convention of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. Suppose $H_{\phi_s}(\omega)\geq-B_sN(\omega)$ and $\phi_r(x)\geq\delta>0$ for $|x|_\infty\leq r_0$, with $\phi_r\geq0$ elsewhere. For the unit cells $C_i=i+[0,1)^d$, there are constants $A>0$ and $B\geq0$ such that every finite configuration satisfies
$$H_\phi(\omega)\geq A\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}N_{C_i}(\omega)^2-BN(\omega).$$
Only finitely many summands are nonzero. This is the cell form used in the continuum pressure arguments.
lem-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field-st:
## Statement

For $L>0$ and a finite configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$ with $N(\omega)=N$, the measure $R_{L,\omega}$ of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]] is a stationary probability law of finite intensity and
$$\rho(R_{L,\omega})=\frac{N}{L^d}.$$
For any probability law $C_L$ on finite configurations in $\Lambda_L$ with $E_{C_L}N<\infty$, its empirical-field barycenter $\bar C_L$ is also a stationary probability law of finite intensity and $\rho(\bar C_L)=E_{C_L}N/L^d$.
lem-tdmath-superquadratic-positive-core:
## Statement

Assume the potential of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]] is stable and regular. In addition, assume either (i) $\chi:(0,r_1]\to(0,\infty)$ is finite-valued and nonincreasing, $\phi(x)\geq\chi(|x|_\infty)$ for $0<|x|_\infty\leq r_1$, and $\int_0^{r_1}\chi(r)r^{d-1}dr=+\infty$; or (ii) there is a hard-core radius $r_h>0$ such that $\phi(x)=+\infty$ whenever $|x|_\infty<r_h$. Then there are a nonnegative nondecreasing $h:\mathbb N_0\to[0,+\infty]$ with $h(0)=0$ and $h(N)/N^2\to+\infty$, and a constant $b<\infty$, such that
$$H_\phi(\omega)\geq\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}h(N_{C_i}(\omega))-bN(\omega).$$
The hard-core alternative permits $h(N)=+\infty$ above the finite packing capacity of a unit cell. This is stronger than ordinary superstability and is not inferred from stability or regularity alone.
thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-li:
## Statement

Let $\phi$ be stable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], fix $\beta>0$, and define $Z(L,N;\beta)$ as in that definition. For sequences $L_j\to\infty$ and integers $N_j\geq0$ with $N_j/L_j^d\to\rho$, define
$$b(\rho)=\sup\left\{\limsup_{j\to\infty}L_j^{-d}\log Z(L_j,N_j;\beta):\frac{N_j}{L_j^d}\to\rho\right\}.$$
Let $F$ be the concave envelope of $b$ on $[0,\infty)$, namely the supremum of $\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i b(\rho_i)$ over finite lists with $\theta_i\geq0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$, $\rho_i\geq0$, and $\sum_i\theta_i\rho_i=\rho$; the empty supremum is $-\infty$. On the interior of $\{\rho:F(\rho)>-\infty\}$, $F$ is finite and continuous. For every $\rho>0$ in that interior and every such sequence $(L_j,N_j)$,
$$\lim_{j\to\infty}L_j^{-d}\log Z(L_j,N_j;\beta)=F(\rho).$$
No claim is made at a close-packing endpoint or at any other excluded endpoint.
thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-fr:
## Statement

Let $\phi$ be stable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], with stability constant $B$, and fix $a,\beta>0$. For free-boundary cubes define $\Xi_L(a,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}a^NZ(L,N;\beta)$. Then
$$1\leq\Xi_L(a,\beta)\leq\exp(ae^{\beta B}L^d),\qquad p(a,\beta):=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log\Xi_L(a,\beta)$$
exists and is finite. This theorem assumes only stability and the decreasing integrable two-sided tail in regularity; it does not assert canonical fixed-density convergence, periodic-boundary equality, or arbitrary-region limits.
thm-tdmath-canonical-grand-duality:
## Statement

Let $F_\beta$ be the finite concave canonical rate on the interior attainable-density interval from [[thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-limit]]. Extend it by $F_\beta(0)=0$, by its interior upper-semicontinuous limit at any finite upper endpoint of its effective domain, and by $-\infty$ outside the closed effective domain; retain the value $-\infty$ if the endpoint limit is $-\infty$. For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, define
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log\Xi_L(e^\alpha,\beta),$$
whose existence is [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]]. Then
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\sup_{\rho\geq0}\bigl(F_\beta(\rho)+\alpha\rho\bigr),\qquad F_\beta(\rho)=\inf_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}\bigl(P(\alpha,\beta)-\alpha\rho\bigr)$$
for every $\rho$ in the closed effective domain of $F_\beta$. These are thermodynamic limits of positional partition functions. They do not assert local-observable equivalence, a finite-volume endpoint realization, or a thin energy-shell limit.
thm-tdmath-superstable-van-hove-pressure:
## Statement

Assume a superstable regular pair potential as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]] and the van Hove definition [[def-tdmath-van-hove-sequence]]. For every van Hove sequence $(\Omega_k)$, the free-wall physical grand pressure satisfies
$$|\Omega_k|^{-1}\log\Xi_{\Omega_k}(z,\beta)\longrightarrow p(z,\beta),$$
the free-cube limit from [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]]. The extra superstability hypothesis is essential to this proof's uniform cell-occupation bound; no arbitrary-shape theorem under stability alone is claimed.
thm-tdmath-uniform-tempered-exterior-pre:
## Statement

Assume a stable regular pair potential with the genuine positive-core condition of [[lem-tdmath-superquadratic-positive-core]]: a nonincreasing $\chi(r)>0$ satisfies $\phi(x)\geq\chi(|x|_\infty)$ near zero and $\int_0^{r_0}\chi(r)r^{d-1}dr=\infty$. For fixed $z,\beta>0$, define the exterior class
$$\Omega(t)=\{\zeta:\sum_{i\in\Lambda_n\cap\mathbb Z^d}N_{C_i}(\zeta)^2\leq t(2n+1)^d\text{ for every }n\}.$$
Then the free-wall grand pressure in $\Lambda_n=[-n-\tfrac12,n+\tfrac12)^d$, with the exterior pair energy against any $\zeta\in\Omega(t)$, converges to the free-cube pressure uniformly in $\zeta$. This statement is conditional on the genuine positive core; it does not infer that condition from superstability alone.
thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressur:
## Statement

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB. Let $\phi$ be superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and fix $z,\beta>0$. For stationary finite-intensity configuration laws, let $I(P)$ be relative entropy density with respect to the independent unit-intensity Poisson law, $\rho(P)=E_PN_{[0,1)^d}$, and $\Phi(P)$ the limiting positional energy density. The existence and lower semicontinuity of $\Phi$ under these hypotheses are part of the proof below. For free and periodic cubes define
$$Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}\!\left[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,bc}}\right],\qquad bc\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}.$$
Then the limit $p_Q(z,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}$ exists, is independent of $bc$, and
$$p_Q(z,\beta)=-\min_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in the local-tame topology $\tau_L$. This theorem concerns positional configurations only. If $\Xi_{L,z,\beta}$ is instead normalized against Lebesgue measure with $1/N!$, then $\Xi_{L,z,\beta}=e^{L^d}Z_{L,z,\beta,\mathrm{free}}$, so its logarithmic rate is $p_Q+1$.
thm-tdmath-van-hove-fixed-n-limit:
## Statement

Assume superstability and regularity, let $(\Omega_k)$ be van Hove, and let $N_k/|\Omega_k|\to\rho$ for an interior attainable density $\rho>0$. For the free-wall exact-$N_k$ positional partition with $1/N_k!$ normalization,
$$|\Omega_k|^{-1}\log Z(\Omega_k,N_k;\beta)\longrightarrow F_\beta(\rho),$$
the free-cube canonical rate of [[thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-limit]]. Superstability is used for the arbitrary-shape pressure upper bound; no stability-only upper theorem is asserted.
lem-tdmath-canonical-empirical-field-con:
## Statement

Let $\beta,z>0$, let $\rho>0$ be an interior attainable density, and choose $\alpha=\log z$ supporting the free canonical rate $F_\beta$ at $\rho$. For either free or periodic boundary condition $b$, let $C^b_{L,N_L}$ be the exact-$N_L$ canonical law and $G^b_{L,z,\beta}$ the grand-canonical law using the same finite-volume energy, where $N_L/L^d\to\rho$. Assume
$$L^{-d}\log Z_b(L,N_L;\beta)\longrightarrow F_\beta(\rho).$$
Let $R_{L,\omega}$ be the periodized empirical field of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]], and let
$$\mathcal M_{z,\beta}:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
Then for every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood $U$ of $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}$ there is $c_U>0$ such that
$$\limsup_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log C^b_{L,N_L}\{\,\omega:R_{L,\omega}\notin U\,\}\leq-c_U.$$
If $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}=\{P_*\}$, then $R_{L,\omega}\to P_*$ in probability in $\tau_L$ under $C^b_{L,N_L}$. This is a statement about spatially averaged local observables through the empirical field, not about the raw finite-box law at a fixed origin.
thm-tdmath-fixed-n-local-ensemble-equiva:
## Statement

Assume the superstable regular model of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]], $\beta>0$, and an interior attainable density $\rho>0$. Let $N_L/L^d\to\rho$, let $C_{L,N_L}$ be the free-boundary positional canonical law with exactly $N_L$ particles, and let $R_{L,\omega}$ be its periodized empirical field from [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]]. Choose any finite supporting activity $z>0$ of $F_\beta$ at $\rho$ and set
$$\mathcal M_{z,\beta}:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
For every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood $U$ of $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}$,
$$C_{L,N_L}\{\omega:R_{L,\omega}\in U\}\longrightarrow1.$$
If $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}=\{P_*\}$, then $R_{L,\omega}\to P_*$ in probability in $\tau_L$. This is local observable equivalence for a uniformly sampled bulk location; it makes no claim about the raw finite-box law at a fixed origin or about uniqueness for every interaction.
lem-tdmath-periodic-law-local-tame-trans:
## Statement

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB as in [[thm-tdmath-local-tame-entropy-compactness]]. Let $L\to\infty$ and let $C_L$ be probability laws on finite configurations in $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, invariant under every translation modulo $L\mathbb Z^d$. Write $Q_L$ for unit-intensity Poisson measure and suppose
$$c_L=L^{-d}D(C_L\Vert Q_L),\qquad \sup_L c_L<\infty.$$
Let $\widetilde C_L$ be the law of the periodic continuation. Then $\widetilde C_L=E_{C_L}R_{L,\omega}$; these laws are stationary and are relatively sequentially compact in $\tau_L$ as $L\to\infty$. Their local counts are uniformly integrable. Along any convergent subsequence with limit $P$,
$$I(P)\leq\liminf_L c_L.$$
If the empirical fields $R_{L,\omega}$ converge in probability in $\tau_L$ to a fixed $P_*$, then $\widetilde C_L\to P_*$ in $\tau_L$, including expectations of every measurable local $f$ with $|f|\leq b(1+N_A)$ for bounded $A$. This concerns periodic continuation, not the zero extension of a configuration outside its fundamental cube.
thm-tdmath-retained-hard-zero-beta-limit:
## Statement

Let $\phi$ be superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and let $B=\{x:\phi(x)=+\infty\}$. For a finite configuration $\omega$, call it admissible when no pair displacement belongs to $B$; for periodic boxes require this also for every periodic image pair. Define the zero-inverse-temperature-parameter continuation (the mathematical $\beta=0$ branch) to be $z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf 1_{\rm admissible}(\omega)$, explicitly retaining the hard exclusion. Then the normalized Poisson free and periodic partition rates exist and equal
$$-\min_{P\in\mathcal K_B}\{I(P)-\rho(P)\log z\},$$
where $\mathcal K_B$ is the set of stationary laws with no forbidden pair almost surely. The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in $\tau_L$. The periodically continued grand laws are relatively compact in $\tau_L$, all their accumulation points are minimizers, and if this minimizer is unique they converge to it for every measurable local observable of at-most-linear count growth. If $B=\varnothing$, this is the Poisson activity-$z$ model. For $B\ne\varnothing$, it is not an unrestricted Poisson law and does not assign a value to the undefined product $0\cdot(+\infty)$.
thm-tdmath-interval-event-ensemble-limit:
## Statement

Assume the superstable regular model and Poisson conventions of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]]. Let $D\subset[0,\infty)$ be an interval of positive length, let $\nu$ be the supremum of finite-entropy, finite-energy attainable densities, and set $e_0(\rho)=\inf\{\Phi(P):\rho(P)=\rho,\ I(P)<\infty\}$. If $\inf D<\nu$ and $e>\inf_{\rho\in D}e_0(\rho)$, define
$$A_L=\{N_{\Lambda_L}/L^d\in D,\ H_{L,\mathrm{per}}/L^d\leq e\}.$$
Then $A_L$ has positive Poisson probability for all sufficiently large $L$, and
$$\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Q_{\Lambda_L}(A_L) =-\min\{I(P):\rho(P)\in\overline D,\ \Phi(P)\leq e\}.$$
Let $R_{L,\omega}$ be the periodized empirical field of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]]. There are $\beta\geq0$ and $z>0$ such that the empirical fields under the conditional law $Q_{\Lambda_L}(\cdot\mid A_L)$ and the matching periodic grand-canonical law concentrate in every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood of the common minimizer set of $I+\beta\Phi-\rho\log z$ when $\beta>0$. At $\beta=0$, retain the forbidden-pair set $B=\{x:\phi(x)=+\infty\}$ and use $I-\rho\log z$ on the hard-admissible stationary class $\mathcal K_B$, with grand weight $z^N\mathbf1_{\rm admissible}$; no value is assigned to $0\cdot(+\infty)$. If this minimizer is unique, both empirical fields converge to it in probability in $\tau_L$. These are empirical-field conclusions. The periodically continued conditional and grand laws also converge in $\tau_L$ under the same uniqueness assumption, for all measurable local observables of at-most-linear count growth. The energy constraint is an upper event and $D$ is nondegenerate; this does not assert exact $N$, a shrinking shell, or a singular energy surface.
thm-tdmath-periodic-fixed-n-limit:
## Statement

Assume the superstable regular interaction of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]], $\beta>0$, and an interior attainable density $\rho>0$. For integers $N_L$ with $N_L/L^d\to\rho$, let $Z_{\mathrm{per}}(L,N_L;\beta)$ be the $1/N_L!$-normalized positional partition on the periodized cube, with the image convention of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. Then
$$L^{-d}\log Z_{\mathrm{per}}(L,N_L;\beta)\longrightarrow F_\beta(\rho),$$
the same rate as the free cube. Let $C^{\mathrm{per}}_{L,N_L}$ be the periodic exact-$N_L$ canonical law and $R_{L,\omega}$ its periodized empirical field from [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]]. For any finite supporting activity $z>0$ of $F_\beta$ at $\rho$, these empirical fields concentrate in every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood of the minimizer set of $I+\beta\Phi-\rho\log z$. A singleton minimizer gives convergence in probability in $\tau_L$.
thm-tdmath-controlled-shell-three-ensemb:
## Statement

Assume the superstable regular model of [[thm-tdmath-periodic-fixed-n-limit]], an interior density $N_L/L^d\to\rho$, and differentiability of $\beta\mapsto F_\beta(\rho)$ at $\beta>0$. Put $e=-\partial_\beta F_\beta(\rho)$. Suppose the grand variational minimizer at a supporting activity $z>0$ is a singleton $P_*$. Let $R_{L,\omega}$ be the periodized empirical field of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]]. There exists a specified sequence $\delta_L\downarrow0$ such that the uniform positional shell law
$$Q_{\Lambda_L}\!\left(\,\cdot\ \middle|\ N=N_L,\ \left|H_{L,\mathrm{per}}/L^d-e\right|\leq\delta_L\right)$$
is eventually defined, and its empirical field converges in probability in $\tau_L$ to $P_*$. The free and periodic exact-$N$ canonical empirical fields and the matching periodic grand-canonical empirical field converge in probability to the same limit. The energy width $2\delta_LL^d=o(L^d)$; no arbitrary prescribed width or zero-width surface measure is asserted.
